prompt:
Game map background for a 2D top-down RPG, 1536x1024 landscape (3:2), filling the whole frame edge to edge, no border.

CAMERA: high-angle bird's-eye view looking down at about 50 degrees, orthographic-looking like a classic JRPG / Stardew-style town map: NO vanishing point, NO perspective convergence, all vertical building edges parallel and pointing straight up the image, ground plane seen almost from above. Building fronts are visible as short facades along the top and side edges; we see their roofs foreshortened. Consistent scale: a doorway is about 60 px wide and 100 px tall, a person would be about 90 px tall (but draw NO people).

STYLE: hand-painted cartoon illustration in exactly the painting style of the attached reference map (clean dark ink outlines on every shape, soft painterly cel shading, natural proportions, rich but slightly muted colours, no chibi, no pixel art, no 3D render, no photo). Mood and palette from the attached stage backdrop: Cyberpunk underground city in the year 2086, night-blue shadows, rusty metal, corrugated sheet metal, cables, steam, wet ground with reflections, neon light in hot pink, cyan and violet, warm yellow window light as accent. Readable game art: the walkable ground is large, flat, clearly lit and uncluttered; props sit at the edges; strong value contrast between floor (walkable) and walls/props (blocking).

The attached images are references for painting style, camera angle, scale and colour ONLY. Do not copy their buildings or layout and do not draw any characters.

STRICT: no people, no figures, no animals, no silhouettes of persons, no readable text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no signature, no frame, no UI.

LOCATION: Follow the layout of the attached grey blockout sketch: light = walkable ground, dark = buildings/blocking, cyan = exits. "Datentunnel", a narrow underground data and supply tunnel system below the city, seen from above. Flat dark concrete tunnel floors with metal floor plates are the walkable area: one long horizontal tunnel across the lower middle of the image from the left edge to the right, one long horizontal tunnel across the upper part, two vertical connecting tunnels on the left and on the right, and a round chamber in the middle connecting them. Bundles of fiber-optic cables run along every tunnel wall and glow in travelling waves of cyan, green and violet light, reflected on the slightly wet floor.
CENTER: in the middle of the round chamber stands the network node - the most eye-catching spot: a tree made of thousands of glowing cables and fibers growing up from the floor, branching into the ceiling, its trunk wrapped with blinking junction boxes, light pulsing up its branches in cyan and green; a small hacking terminal at its foot.
TOP: along the upper tunnel's top wall a row of server racks in wall niches, blinking with tiny lights, some doors hanging open, a loudspeaker horn mounted high on the wall.
TOP LEFT: a vertical cable shaft - a square opening going up with a steel ladder and thick cables disappearing upwards.
TOP RIGHT: a narrow maintenance ladder going straight up to a round hatch in the ceiling, a small cold white lamp above it.
LEFT EDGE, lower tunnel: a heavy round steel bulkhead door with a big turning wheel set into the wall at the left edge.
RIGHT EDGE middle: a small dead-end niche full of broken monitors and cracked server parts glowing faintly green.
BOTTOM CENTER: a small niche with drone docking racks and a charging station.
BOTTOM RIGHT: a small corner niche where an old antenna pokes through a crack in the ceiling, a tangle of wires and a little folding chair.
BOTTOM LEFT: solid concrete and server room walls (blocking).
Cables drawn thin so they don't hide the floor, a few warning stripes, steam from a vent, puddles.
EXITS clearly readable at the image edges: LEFT edge - the round bulkhead door with the turning wheel; TOP LEFT - the cable shaft with the ladder going up; TOP RIGHT - the maintenance ladder to the ceiling hatch.
Time: always night underground, dark blue shadows, lit by the glowing fiber cables, the network node and small lamps.
